jobs.title: Hazardous Waste Handler- Floater (Insite Chemist)
jobs.description:
Hazardous Waste Handler – Floater

Location: San Diego, CA

Pay: $25–$30 per hour

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–4:00 PM

CDL: Not required

Mileage: Reimbursed

Position Overview

We are seeking a dependable, positive, self-motivated Hazardous Waste Handler to service multiple client locations throughout San Diego County, including La Jolla, Carlsbad, Escondido, Oceanside, and Rancho Bernardo.

This is a hands-on, general labor and environmental services position. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who takes initiative, works independently, has a strong work ethic, and enjoys interacting with customers.

This is NOT a laboratory or chemist position. The role focuses on general labor, hazardous waste management, regulatory compliance, customer service, and facility inspections.

Key Responsibilities

Perform hands-on general labor and hazardous waste handling.
Manage, organize, label, segregate, and maintain hazardous waste in accordance with applicable regulations.
Monitor waste accumulation areas and ensure compliance with RCRA and other applicable environmental requirements.
Conduct routine facility inspections and identify potential compliance issues.
Maintain accurate inspection records, waste logs, and required documentation.
Service client locations and maintain positive customer relationships.
Communicate professionally with customers regarding waste management needs and compliance concerns.
Identify issues, take initiative, and help resolve problems.
Maintain clean, organized, and compliant waste storage areas.
Travel between multiple customer sites throughout the assigned service territory.

Ideal Candidate

Positive attitude and professional demeanor.
Self-starter with strong self-motivation.
Dependable, punctual, and organized.
Comfortable performing physical, hands-on general labor.
Able to work independently and manage multiple client locations.
Strong customer service and communication skills.
Detail-oriented with the ability to recognize compliance issues.
Takes ownership of responsibilities and follows through on tasks.
Willingness to learn environmental regulations and waste management procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

40-Hour HAZWOPER certification.
RCRA training or experience.
Previous hazardous waste handling experience.
Environmental services or industrial general labor experience.
Experience conducting inspections and maintaining compliance documentation.

Clean Harbors is looking for Chemical Handlers to join our safety conscious team!  

Do you enjoy...    

Staying active and on your feet?
Learning and applying knowledge about science and chemistry? 
Working directly with customers?

Why work for Clean Harbors?

Health and Safety is our #1 priority, and we live it 3-6-5!  
Competitive wages and generous paid time off
Comprehensive health benefits coverage after 30 days of full-time employment
Group 401K/RRSP with company matching component
Company paid training and tuition reimbursement
Company provided vehicles and equipment
Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career!

Responsibilities

Wondering what to expect in starting a career at Clean Harbors?

InSite Technicians perform a wide range of tasks, including: 

Making waste pickups throughout a customer’s facility;
Conducting chemical bulking and consolidation;
Packaging and labeling waste products to maximize efficiency and maintain compliance;
Participating in spill response on customer’s site as needed;
Operating forklifts;
Inspecting drums for container integrity and regulatory compliance;
Ensuring the safe loading and unloading of waste hauling vehicles; 
Completing waste stream sampling and profiling. 

This position is an entry level role, but many of our leaders started in this job! With safety as our top priority, you'll get the training and support to not only succeed at your job but advance your career.

Qualifications

What does it take to work for Clean Harbors? 

High School diploma or equivalent; 
Valid driver’s license; 
Grade 4 Industrial Wastewater License preferred;
Willingness to complete a background check, drug test, and physical. 

To learn more about Clean Harbors, and to view and apply online for exciting opportunities in our company, visit us at https://careers.cleanharbors.com/   

Clean Harbors 
is the leading provider of environmental, energy, and industrial services throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico. Our mission is to create a safer, cleaner environment through the treatment, recycling, and disposal of hazardous materials. Come help us save the world! 

Clean Harbors is an equal opportunity employer.

Please be advised that Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support certain stages of the recruitment process but are not used as a replacement for human decision making.

Clean Harbors is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact ect@cleanharbors.com or 1-844-922-5547.

Clean Harbors is a Military & Veteran friendly company.

Clean Harbors is committed to complying with applicable pay transparency laws and ensuring fair and equitable compensation. The posted salary range reflects the minimum and maximum target for this role. Final compensation may vary based on factors such as location, experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to the base salary, some roles may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.description:
Environmental Science Expert - $90/hr Remote - Alignerr

Location: Remote

About The Job

At Alignerr, we partner with the world’s leading AI research teams and labs to build and train cutting-edge AI models.

Organization
: Alignerr Position
: Environmental Science Expert (Masters/PhDs) Type
: Hourly Contract Compensation
: $75–$90 /hour Location
: Remote Commitment
: 10–40 hours/week

Develop, solve, and review advanced environmental science problems with real-world relevance.

jobs.title: Environmental Science Expert (Masters/PhDs)
jobs.description:
Environmental Science Expert (AI Training)

About The Role

What if your expertise in climate modeling, ecology, or sustainability could directly shape how AI understands and reasons about the most pressing environmental challenges facing our planet? We're looking for Environmental Science experts to develop and review advanced, real-world problems that teach AI systems to think with genuine scientific rigor.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role built for researchers and advanced degree holders who want to put their domain expertise to meaningful use — on their own schedule.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Design, solve, and review complex environmental science problems with real-world relevance — spanning climate modeling, ecology, sustainability, and related disciplines
Apply your advanced domain knowledge to craft challenging, nuanced problem statements that push AI reasoning to its limits
Evaluate AI-generated outputs for scientific accuracy, depth, and rigor
Collaborate asynchronously with AI researchers and fellow domain experts to refine and improve model performance
Ensure clarity, precision, and intellectual integrity across all deliverables
Work independently on task-based assignments fully on your own schedule

Who You Are

Hold a Master's or PhD in Environmental Science or a closely related field
Deep expertise in at least one of: climate modeling, ecology, environmental sustainability, or adjacent areas
Proficient in Python or R for research, data analysis, or scientific computing
Exceptional written communicator — you can translate complex science into clear, well-structured problem statements
Detail-oriented, rigorous, and comfortable working independently
Fluent in English and based in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Australia, or New Zealand

Nice to Have

Prior experience with data annotation, data labeling, or AI evaluation workflows
Background in interdisciplinary research spanning environmental science and quantitative modeling
Experience designing curriculum, assessments, or research problems in an academic or professional setting
Familiarity with AI tools or large language model capabilities

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Freelance autonomy with the structure of meaningful, expert-level work
Make a direct impact on how AI understands environmental science and reasons about climate and ecology
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

jobs.title: Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
Environmental Health Officers

Multiple Opportunities Available | Full-Time & Part-Time Options

Join a progressive and evolving Environmental Health team committed to protecting public health, supporting local businesses, and delivering positive outcomes for our community. Whether you're completing your studies, recently graduated, or an experienced Environmental Health Officer looking for your next challenge, we have a range of opportunities available to suit your experience and career stage.

Choose the opportunity that suits you

Environmental Health Officer (Graduate Progression) – Level 3
10-month fixed-term contract
Available on a full-time or part-time basis
Ideal for someone completing an environmental health qualification or a graduate building their experience
A supported opportunity to develop practical skills across a broad range of environmental health functions
Salary of $92,318 per annum plus Superannuation

Environmental Health Officer – Level 5
Ongoing position
Multiple opportunities available
Available on a full-time or part-time basis
Suited to an experienced and confident officer who can manage a varied workload with greater autonomy
Salary of $103,808 per annum plus Superannuation

About Us

At the City of Port Adelaide Enfield (PAE), we’re building a welcoming, liveable city, made by people.

Our focus is on community, our economy, environmental sustainability and building high-quality places for people to enjoy. We’re on an ambitious trajectory, but our organisation is up for the challenge.

At PAE, we’re involved in all sorts of things - major construction through to environmental management, organising events, social infrastructure planning, and library services. We are proud of offering a wide range of accessible services and programs to our community.
You don’t need experience in local government for this role - we’re looking for transferrable skills and a great attitude.

Now’s a great time to be part of PAE.

About the Roles

We're reshaping our Environmental Health service to be more agile, risk-based and outcomes focused. This is an exciting time to join a team that embraces innovation, values fresh ideas and is committed to finding better ways to serve our growing community.

As an Environmental Health Officer, you will help protect and promote community health by providing professional advice, undertaking inspections and investigations, and supporting compliance with relevant public and environmental health requirements. Depending on your classification, you will work with an appropriate level of support or autonomy while delivering practical, education-focused and proportionate regulatory outcomes. If you are still completing your studies, your duties will initially focus on food safety inspections, with your responsibilities growing as you complete your qualification and gain further experience and knowledge.

What you will do

Undertake inspections, assessments and investigations across a range of environmental and public health matters
Provide clear, practical advice to residents, businesses and other stakeholders
Apply relevant legislation, policies and procedures fairly and consistently
Prepare accurate records, correspondence and reports
Support education, prevention and compliance initiatives that contribute to positive community outcomes
Work collaboratively with colleagues and internal and external stakeholders

About You

You will hold, or be working towards, an appropriate qualification in environmental health (refer to this link for qualification requirements > Local Authorised Officer Approved Qualification List) and bring a genuine commitment to protecting community wellbeing. You will communicate respectfully, exercise sound judgement and take a constructive approach to education and compliance.

For the graduate opportunity, you may be completing an environmental health qualification or be a graduate who is ready to learn, welcomes guidance and is keen to build confidence in a supportive team environment.

For the skilled officer opportunity, you will bring demonstrated environmental health experience, sound regulatory judgement and the ability to independently manage complex or sensitive matters while supporting consistent team outcomes.

Why join us?

Meaningful work that directly supports community health and wellbeing
A collaborative and knowledgeable team environment
Professional development and exposure to varied environmental health matters
Flexibility to consider full-time or part-time arrangements for the ongoing Level 5 role
An inclusive workplace that values different perspectives and experiences

More information can be found in the Position Description located below.

At PAE, our values guide us to work together, strive for improvement, and make a positive impact in our community. We seek people who share these values.
#bettertogether #growandimprove #makeadifference.

We value diversity and inclusion, and we encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Apply Now

To apply, simply complete the application process by clicking the ‘Apply’ button and attach your cover letter and resume.

When submitting your application, please indicate whether you wish to be considered for:
Graduate / Emerging Environmental Health Officer
Experienced Environmental Health Officer
Or both

Applications close 10:00pm on Sunday 8 November 2026

We’re committed to an accessible, inclusive workplace and welcome discussions about any adjustments you may need.

The City of PAE is located on Kaurna Country. We acknowledge the Kaurna people as the traditional custodians of the Adelaide region and extend our respect to custodians and Elders who have passed, those amongst us and those emerging.
